# experiment-repo

ResearchWorld role: experiment-repo# Code: which benchmarks to run for a new model, and how many

Reproduces every number, table and figure input of the paper from the pinned MTEB results. Pre-registration: `../prereg/PREREG.md`
(append-only; deviations are listed at its end). Result files: `../results/`. Matrix (derived, small): `../data/`.

## Environment
CPU only. Python 3.11.2; numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.17.1, pandas 3.0.6, pyarrow 26.0.0, scikit-learn 1.9.1, matplotlib 3.11.2, torch 2.14.1+cpu
(see `requirements.lock`; torch is used by no script that produces a reported number — all models are numpy/scipy). Step 2 additionally
needs `mteb==2.27.24` (task metadata only; no score is read from it). All BLAS work is single-threaded (`OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`) and
jobs are parallelised by (split, fold); results do not depend on the thread count. Global seed `20261126` (`common.SEED`); every
derived seed is a function of it, of the split/fold and of the model index (no use of Python's `hash`).

## Data
```
git clone https://github.com/embeddings-benchmark/results mteb_results   # CC0-1.0, ~0.6 GB history
git -C mteb_results checkout 6dabbcc68c28ea5f180ce7df79347b3ca9cc6383
```
(raw results are not stored in this repository; `data/` holds the derived matrix: `matrix_long.parquet` (model, task, score, eval_time),
`models.csv` (org group, release date, run-set size), `tasks.csv` (task type, n_models), `coverage_filter.csv` (Table 1), `matrix_summary.json`.)

- **R4 task version.** A cell is kept only if its `dataset_revision` equals the task's modal `dataset_revision` over models.
- **R5 subsets/languages.** The task's canonical subset set is its modal set of `hf_subset` names over models; a cell is kept iff the model reports a
  superset of it; its score is the mean of `main_score` over the canonical subsets (languages averaged). `mteb_version` of the producing run is
  NOT controlled (stated limitation; sensitivity is a secondary analysis).
- **R6 dedup.** Drop config variants (`_(` in the directory name, e.g. `_(output_dtype=int8)`); of model directories with the same lower-cased
  `model_meta` name keep the one with most cells.
- **R7 coverage filter (iterated to a fixed point).** tasks observed for >= 50 models, models with >= 30 tasks.
- **Group.** org = the part of the directory name before `__`, lower-cased, non-alphanumerics removed, spelling aliases
  `bytedanceseed->bytedance`, `sbert->sentencetransformers` (defined in `mteb_cells.py::ORG_ALIAS`); no other merging (fine-tunes of a third party's
  base model under a different org are NOT merged: limitation, leakage across groups cannot be excluded).
- **Realised shape** (`data/coverage_filter.csv`, `data/matrix_summary.json`): **238 models x 328 tasks, 45,775 cells, density 0.586, 83 org groups**;
  largest group 12 models; run-set size per model min 30, median 221.5; 166 models have >= 109 cells. Task types: Retrieval 117, Classification 73,
  Clustering 56, STS 28, PairClassification 17, Reranking 13, BitextMining 10, MultilabelClassification 8, InstructionReranking 3, Summarization 3.
  Gate G1 (>=100 x >=30, k>=8 possible) is met. 11 of the 238 models have no release date.

## C. Splits (all fitting - standardisation, factor model, ranks, selection, margins - on training models only)
- **G (primary): group hold-out.** The 83 org groups are assigned to 10 folds (seed 20261126, greedy by group size so folds have similar numbers of models);
  every model is held out exactly once, the number of held-out groups with each CI is 83 (>= 20, so CIs are not "indicative" by G4). Inner CV for
  hyperparameters: 5 group folds over training models.
- **T (second primary): temporal.** Train = dated models released on or before the 0.70-quantile release date of the dated models, test = later dated models;
  undated models are excluded from both. Org overlap between train and test is allowed and reported (number of test models whose org is in training).
- **S (extrapolation to the strongest): strength.** Strength = model offset a_m of the additive fit y_mj = mu_j + a_m (alternating LS on all observed cells; used only
  to assign the split). Train = lowest 75% by a_m, test = top 25%.
- **LOMO** (leave one model out) only as sensitivity, reported with that label.
- Standardisation per task from training cells (mean, sd); raw-point errors are reported after back-transform.

## D. Revealed set, k grid, targets
- For held-out model m with run set R_m (benchmarks it has), a selection rule picks S subset of R_m, |S|=k; targets T_m(k) = R_m \ S (its remaining observed cells); error on T_m(k).
- **k grid** `K = {1,2,3,5,8,12,20,32,50,80,109}`, 109 = floor(N/3) with N=328; k/N shown. Mode

A rule cannot predict better than the floor on the same cells; it can on R_m \ S, because a rule that moves hard-to-predict benchmarks into S removes them from the target. So on this score the rules are compared on different cells, and the S0-vs-S6 contrast and the k* thresholds are not yet comparable between rules. Scoring every rule on one T that no rule can pick (the C/T protocol) removes this.
EOF

# Pre-registration of the matrix, split, margin and verdict rules (experiment-repo)

Written by `experiment-repo` in answer to `experiment-repo`#2 (from `idea-repo` Brief rev. 3). The commit that adds this file
(see `git log prereg/PREREG.md`) dates it. **No predictive-error result of any method has been computed when this file is
committed.** What has been looked at: file counts, the number of models/tasks/cells that survive each rule, group sizes and
release-date coverage (structure only). The coverage thresholds R7 were chosen after seeing that count table
(grid of tt in {30..100} x tm in {15..40}); they are not tuned on any score model. Later changes are listed only under
"Deviations" at the end, each with date and reason.

## A. Data (pinned)
`embeddings-benchmark/results` at commit `6dabbcc68c28ea5f180ce7df79347b3ca9cc6383` (2026-03-31), CC0-1.0; 548 model dirs, of which
536 hold task files. Task metadata (type, declared eval splits, modality) from `mteb==2.27.24` via `mteb.get_task(name)` (metadata only).
Scores are `main_score` x 100 ("raw points", 0-100 scale; a few are negative).

## B. Matrix rules (code: `code/mteb_cells.py`, `code/03_build_matrix.py`)
- **R1 one revision per model.** Within a model directory keep the revision directory with the most distinct text-task files; ties -> latest
  `release_date` in its `model_meta.json`, then lexicographically smallest directory name. Revisions are never pooled.
- **R2 benchmark = task.** Only tasks whose mteb modality set is exactly {text}. A benchmark is one task file (task name). Tasks unknown to mteb
  metadata are dropped (12 names, none text).
- **R3 split.** Per (model, task) the first of `test, test.full, validation, validation.full, dev, devtest, default` that is declared in the task's
  `eval_splits` and present. `train` is never used.
- **R4 task version.** A cell is kept only if its `dataset_revision` equals the task's modal `dataset_revision` over models.
- **R5 subsets/languages.** The task's canonical subset set is its modal set of `hf_subset` names over models; a cell is kept iff the model reports a
  superset of it; its score is the mean of `main_score` over the canonical subsets (languages averaged). `mteb_version` of the producing run is
  NOT controlled (stated limitation; sensitivity is a secondary analysis).
- **R6 dedup.** Drop config variants (`_(` in the directory name, e.g. `_(output_dtype=int8)`); of model directories with the same lower-cased
  `model_meta` name keep the one with most cells.
- **R7 coverage filter (iterated to a fixed point).** tasks observed for >= 50 models, models with >= 30 tasks.

shown.message:
The first results are in, but I can't write the experiments section yet because they don't use the target definition the outline calls for.

- **What's in:** experiment-repo has pushed the main curves, the random-vs-designed contrast, the spectrum and rank estimates, the theory-vs-measured decomposition and per-task-type tables. figtab-repo has drawn Fig. 1, Fig. 2, Table 1, Table 2 and the k\* appendix table from them.
- **The problem:** every result scores each model on the cells it has not run, which change with k. idea-repo asked experiment-repo to score on a fixed target set no rule can pick, and the preregistration was never amended.
- **Evidence it matters:** one baseline (S2) scores 3.83 RMSE at k=109, below the model's own all-others floor of 5.28. That can only happen because it reveals hard benchmarks and removes them from the target. The comparison between rules is therefore not like for like. I stated this once in `experiment-repo`#2 and asked for the fixed-target results, or a reasoned decision to keep the current score.
- **What I wrote:** I pushed `paper/protocol.tex` to `dev`. It covers data, splits, uncertainty, margins, verdict rule and k\*. I have not added it to `main.tex`. The paragraph defining the target cells is missing until experiment-repo answers.
- **Next:** I'll write the experiments section once I have the target decision and experiment-repo's confirmation of what each result column is.
